name: Denmark
summary: Euphoriant Substances Act (lists A–E): possession for own use is an offence, usually a fixed fine set in law since July 2025; above set amounts means prison. Supervised drug consumption rooms are legal.
callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan law. Health staff are bound by confidentiality. Since July 2024, socially marginalised people dependent on hard drugs get a warning, not a fine, for own-use possession.
drugChecking: No established public drug checking service found. Supervised drug consumption rooms operate legally in several cities.

lsd.note: List A. Own-use possession fined (first offence DKK 3,000 for up to 9 doses, rising with amount and repeats).

mushrooms.note: Psilocybin mushrooms and their spores are on List B (since 2001). Own-use possession is fined.

dmt.note: List B. Ayahuasca is illegal; the Supreme Court rejected a religious (Santo Daime) exemption.

mescaline.note: Mescaline and San Pedro/Peruvian torch cacti and seeds (Echinopsis pachanoi/peruviana) are explicitly on List B.

dox.note: DOB, DOM etc. on List B; the phenethylamine group definition covers analogues.

nbomes.note: Covered by the List B phenethylamine group definition (N-methoxybenzyl substitution).

5-meo-xxt.note: 5-MeO-DMT, 5-MeO-DIPT and 5-MeO-DALT are on List B. 5-MeO-MiPT isn't listed by name (2026 order), so its status is unclear.

cannabis.note: Fine DKK 2,000 (<10 g hash/<50 g weed), +50%/+100% for repeats; doubled in strict penalty zones. Christiania's Pusher Street closed 2024.

ketamine.note: List B medicine. Without a prescription, fines like amphetamine: DKK 3,000 (<1 g) to 8,000; 5 g or more means prison.

dxm.note: Prescription-only since 2008. Pure DXM is on List C; ordinary medicines containing it fall outside the narcotics rules.

nitrous.note: Not a narcotic. Since July 2023, possession in public places is banned (fine from DKK 3,000) and sales to under-18s are banned. EU consumer ban due 2027.

amphetamines.note: List B: fines DKK 3,000–8,000 below 5 g (more for repeats); 5 g+ means prison. ADHD medicines legal with a prescription.

mdma.note: List B. Fines: DKK 3,000 (up to 3 pills), 6,000 (4–11), 8,000 (12–19); 20+ pills means prison even for own use.

cocaine.note: List B. Fines DKK 3,000 (<1 g), 6,000 (1–2.9 g), 8,000 (3–4.9 g); 5 g or more means prison.

alcohol.note: Shops may sell drinks up to 6% ABV from 16; stronger drinks from 18 (since April 2025). Bars and restaurants: 18.

ghb/gbl.note: GHB is on List B (fined like other drugs). GBL and 1,4-BD are not on the narcotics lists (2026 order).

opioids.note: Heroin is List A; 5 g+ is always prison. Tougher fines for opioid pills since July 2025 (50+ pills = prison). Legal only with a prescription.

tramadol.note: List B: possession without a prescription is fined as opioid pills (DKK 3,000 for up to 9 pills).

benzodiazepines.note: List E (flunitrazepam List D). Unprescribed possession fined (DKK 3,000 up to 49 pills); 100+ pills means prison.

maois.note: Medical MAOIs are prescription-only, not narcotics. Harmala/Syrian rue are not listed; ayahuasca is illegal because of DMT.

ssris.note: Prescription-only medicines, not narcotics: possession isn't a drug offence, but unauthorised supply is illegal.
